note: Legato through one pentatonic position: a legato-trill on the two notes of the position's G string, then the whole position picked once per string and hammered or pulled to the other note. One position is on the screen, so the title and headings name no number. The trill can't change key, so moves holds only a tempo range.

exercise.title: Legato through an A minor pentatonic position
exercise.why: Every string in a pentatonic position has two notes, so each string can be one picked note and one hammered or pulled note.

cells.heading: The trill on the G string

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}, and follow the tab: pick once, then hammer on and pull off with no more picking.
These are the two notes on the G string of the position in the next tool, so your hand is already where it will play.
Practice until the hammered note is as loud as the picked one.

The neck below shows the A minor pentatonic scale in one position: each dot is a note to play, and the ringed dots are the {{1}} notes. Start on the lowest dot on the low E string and play up to the high e string at your own pace: pick the lower note on each string and hammer on to the higher one. Coming back down, pick the higher note and pull off to the lower one.
Practice until the position is in your muscle memory: your fretting hand hammers and pulls without you thinking about which string comes next.
